status: Research pattern book, 2026-10-26. Classical patterns per life area mined from the OCR of BPHS (Sharma vol.1), Phaladeepika, Saravali, Brihat Jataka and Uttara Kalamritam. Tiers: A = 2+ classics agree and the engine computes it; B = one classic; C = classic, engine missing; H = hypothesis. Source notes: /mnt/project-files/research/ask-patterns/. Not yet validated by a practising astrologer.

question_types: Will I do well in my career?
cards.rule: Find the lord of the 10th house from Lagna. If it is exalted, in its own sign or own navamsa, and strong by Shadbala, the career has fame and solid results. If it is debilitated, combust, or sits in the 6th, 8th or 12th, expect obstruction and slow progress.

sources.location: Ch.23 (Effects of the 10th House) v.2-3, pp.262-263
Adhyaya XX sl.11 and sl.19, pp.204-207

cards.agreement: 3 books agree that the 10th lord's strength decides the career line (BPHS, Phaladeepika, UK); Saravali gives the signification only. No disagreement found.
cards.convention: no (whole-sign houses from Lagna; Bhava-chalit cusp is an alternative, bhava_chalit.bhava_chalit)

question_types: What kind of work suits me?
Where will my money come from?
cards.rule: Look at the 10th house from Lagna and from the Moon (use the stronger of the two). The planet sitting there names the channel of livelihood: Sun = father, state, authority; Moon = mother, public, liquids; Mars = competition, land, engineering, force; Mercury = friends, writing, trade; Jupiter = elders, teaching, advice, finance; Venus = women, arts, luxury; Saturn = labour, service, hard trades.
cards.agreement: 2 books agree word for word (Brihat Jataka, Phaladeepika). BJ's commentator warns that one planet rarely explains a whole livelihood; several channels can run together.
cards.convention: yes: which reference (Lagna or Moon) is stronger; the texts give no fixed rule

question_types: Which profession or field suits me?
Will I work in my home town or away?
cards.rule: If the 10th house is empty, take the 10th lord from Lagna, Moon and Sun (the strongest), see which navamsa it occupies, and read the lord of that navamsa: Sun = state service, medicine, metals, wool; Moon = water trades, farming, textiles, women's goods; Mars = metals, fire, weapons, engineering, bold ventures; Mercury = writing, maths, poetry, arts, trade; Jupiter = teaching, priesthood, law, finance, charities; Venus = gems, silver, cattle, luxury, arts; Saturn = labour, transport, hard crafts. A strong navamsa lord gives earning without strain; a weak one gives little.
cards.agreement: 2 books agree (Phaladeepika restates Brihat Jataka). No disagreement.
cards.convention: yes: strongest of Lagna / Moon / Sun as the reference; Lahiri ayanamsa shifts navamsa for planets near a 3°20' boundary

cards.rule: In the Jaimini system the Amatyakaraka (the planet with the second-highest degree in its sign) stands for the profession. Its nature, sign and dignity colour the work; its dasha and transits time career events.
cards.agreement: 1 book states the profession use (UK); BPHS defines the karaka. Books differ on 7 vs 8 karakas (BPHS lists eight including Pitri; UK lists seven).
cards.convention: yes: 7-karaka vs 8-karaka scheme (Rahu counted in reverse); result can change AmK

question_types: Will my business or trade succeed?
Does my soul-planet support my work?
cards.rule: Find the Karakamsha (the navamsa sign of the Atmakaraka). Look at the 10th sign from it in the navamsa chart. A benefic there or aspecting gives steady wealth and good judgement; a malefic there gives losses in trade; Mercury and Venus there give gains in trade and many achievements; Sun and Moon with Jupiter there give high authority.
cards.agreement: 2 books use the Karakamsha method; only BPHS gives the 10th-from-Karakamsha rule. UK's commentator notes the author seems to count from the Atmakaraka's rasi, not the navamsa.
cards.convention: yes: Karakamsha in D9 (Jaimini/BPHS) vs rasi (UK author); Jaimini rasi-aspect vs Parasari graha-aspect

question_types: Will I hold a position of authority?
cards.rule: When the lord of an angle (1,4,7,10) and the lord of a trine (5,9) join, aspect each other or exchange signs, a Raja Yoga forms: rise in rank, authority and recognition. The 9th-10th and 5th-10th links are strongest. The gains arrive in the dashas of the planets forming the yoga.

sources.location: Kanda 1 ch.4 v.23 and notes, pp.69, 93-94

cards.agreement: 3 books agree. They differ on how wide the net is: UK and PD name 9-10 and 4-9-10 specifically; BPHS accepts any kendra-trikona link, with 5th-10th singled out.
cards.convention: no for the yoga; yes for timing (dasha start variant)

question_types: Will I get a government job?
Is public service or politics for me?
cards.rule: Flags for state or public service (read together, never alone): a strong Sun (dignity and Shadbala); Sun, Moon and Mercury together; the 5th lord in the 10th; the 10th lord in the Sun's navamsa; the 2nd sign from the Atmakaraka holding or aspected by Sun and Venus. A strong Moon points to public or elected roles.
cards.agreement: 4 books carry at least one flag; none contradicts another. 'King/ruler' read as government is a modern gloss and is marked as such.
cards.convention: yes: 'ruler' -> government is interpretive; karaka scheme for AK

question_types: Should I start my own venture?
cards.rule: The classics make the 7th house the house of trade and the 10th the house of rank and service, and they place Mercury and Venus at the 10th from Karakamsha for trade gains. Working rule: a strong 7th lord linked to the 10th or to 2/11, Mercury or Venus strong and linked to the 10th, or Mercury+Venus at the 10th from Karakamsha lean to business; a strong Sun or Saturn ruling or occupying the 10th, with the 6th (service) linked, leans to employment.
cards.agreement: 3 books agree on the house meanings (7th trade, 10th rank/livelihood). The job-vs-business decision rule itself is modern practice, not a classical verse.
cards.convention: yes: the weighting is a modern heuristic; mark as such in answers

question_types: When will I get a job?
cards.rule: Career events cluster in the Vimshottari mahadasha and antardasha of the 10th lord, the Lagna lord, planets in the 10th, and Raja-yoga planets, when those lords are strong. A weak 10th lord's dasha brings fruitless effort and loss of position. Where in the dasha the weight falls follows the lord's drekkana (first third = early, etc.).
cards.agreement: 3 books agree on dasha-of-the-house-lord timing and on strength deciding the sign of the result.
cards.convention: yes: Vimshottari start (Moon nakshatra default vs Kshema/Utpanna/Adhana/Lagna starts) changes the whole timeline; Yogini and Chara are separate systems

question_types: Is this a good time to change jobs?
Why is work hard this year?
cards.rule: Count transits from the natal Moon. Saturn in the 3rd, 6th or 11th and Jupiter in the 2nd, 5th, 7th, 9th or 11th support career moves and gains; Saturn or Mars crossing the 10th, and Jupiter in the 10th, bring strain, loss of honour or failed attempts. A favourable transit is cancelled (vedha) when another planet sits in its vedha house. Raise or lower each verdict by the Ashtakavarga bindus of the sign being transited.
cards.agreement: 2 books agree on Moon-sign gochara modified by Ashtakavarga; UK adds the age-based reference switch, which PD does not have. Brihat Jataka has no gochara chapter.
cards.convention: yes: reference point (Moon vs Lagna vs UK age rule); vedha table variants

question_types: What field is right for me?
Will I gain position and influence?
cards.rule: The Dasamsa (D10) is the division for rank and public action. Read the 10th lord's dignity in D10, the D10 Lagna lord, and planets in the D10 10th house to sharpen the field and the standing the rasi chart promises. Give D10 a lighter weight than the rasi chart.
cards.agreement: 2 books agree on D10's purpose and on giving it less weight than the rasi. The specific D10 reading rules used today are modern practice.
cards.convention: yes: D10 counting (Parasari odd-from-same, even-from-9th is used); Lahiri ayanamsa near 3-degree boundaries

question_types: How will the world see my career?
Will my career succeed after struggle?
cards.rule: Find the Arudha of the 10th (A10, the public image of the career). Strong planets or benefics in angles, trines or upachayas from A10 support visible success; malefics in trines from A10 mean success only after struggle.
cards.agreement: 2 books use arudhas; only UK gives the A10 example. BPHS vol.1 gives the method for AL and A7, not A10 directly.
cards.convention: yes: arudha exception rule (pada in the same sign or 7th moves 10 signs); Jaimini rasi aspects not implemented

question_types: Will I be famous or respected in my work?
cards.rule: Reputation markers: a Pancha Mahapurusha yoga (Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus or Saturn in own or exalted sign in an angle); a benefic in the 10th from Lagna or Moon (Amala yoga); Jupiter in the 10th; the 10th lord exalted in an angle or trine with Jupiter. Each adds to lasting good name rather than raw income.

sources.location: Adhyaya VI sl.1-4, pp.46-49; Adhyaya VIII sl.16, pp.90-92

cards.agreement: 3 books agree on Jupiter/benefic influence on the 10th; Mahapurusha yogas located in PD only this pass (BPHS and Saravali carry them per references.json).

question_types: Why do I keep losing jobs?
cards.rule: Caution flags, never verdicts: the 10th lord in the 6th, 8th or 12th or debilitated; the 8th lord in the 10th without a benefic aspect; Saturn with a debilitated planet in the 10th; Duryoga (lords of 6, 8, 12 strong in angles or trines while lords of 1, 4, 9, 10 are weak in 6/8/12). Each flag is softened by a benefic aspect, a Vipareeta Raja yoga, or a strong Lagna lord.
cards.agreement: 2 books agree on dusthana links spoiling the career; both give cancellations.

cards.rule: When two or more lords of houses 2, 5, 9 and 11 (and the Lagna lord) join, aspect each other or exchange signs, and are strong, a Dhana yoga forms and wealth follows in the dashas of those lords. If a lord of 6, 8 or 12 joins the combination, the gain leaks away into debts and disputes.

sources.location: Ch.15 (Effects of the 2nd House) v.4-5 and examples, pp.203-205

cards.agreement: 3 books agree on the lords-of-wealth-houses method; Saravali adds a benefics-in-upachaya variant that the engine does not compute.
cards.convention: no for the yoga; yes for timing (dasha start)

question_types: Will my family be well off?
cards.rule: The 2nd lord in the 2nd, an angle or a trine supports savings and family wealth; in the 6th, 8th or 12th wealth leaks. An exalted or own-sign 2nd lord gives a generous, respected earner; a 2nd lord with a benefic and in a high varga dignity gives wealth with little effort.

sources.location: Adhyaya XX sl.3 and sl.15, pp.201-206

cards.agreement: 2 books agree. Saravali gives only the signification (2nd = Artha, Dhana).

question_types: Will I get gains from my efforts?
cards.rule: The 11th lord in the 11th, an angle or a trine gives steady gains; exalted, it gives gains even when combust. The 11th lord in the 2nd with the 2nd lord in the 11th gives abundant fortune. The 11th lord fallen, combust, or in 6/8/12 with a malefic is a caution that gains come hard.

sources.location: Ch.24 (11th House) v.2-11 (Santhanam pp.141-143 per references.json); Sharma OCR notes pp.331-332
Adhyaya VIII sl.16, pp.90-92; Adhyaya XXVI sl.2, 22-23

cards.agreement: 3 books agree that the 11th is gains and that benefics there or its lord well placed support income.

question_types: Is Jupiter good for my finances?
cards.rule: Jupiter in the 2nd, 5th, 9th, 10th or 11th from Lagna, or Jupiter as 2nd lord in the 2nd, or Jupiter joined with Mars, is a wealth marker. Jupiter in the 11th with Moon in the 2nd and Venus in the 9th is a named big-gain pattern.

sources.location: Ch.15 v.3 (Santhanam p.96 per references.json) and example chart p.203; Ch.24 v.6 (Santhanam p.142)

cards.agreement: 3 books agree on Jupiter in 9/10/11 as a wealth marker.

question_types: Do I have a strong fortune for wealth?
cards.rule: Lakshmi yoga: the 9th lord in its own or exaltation sign in an angle or trine while the Lagna lord is strong gives lasting wealth and comfort. Also, the 9th lord's dasha brings prosperity and royal favour.

sources.location: Adhyaya VI sl.24, pp.55-58; Adhyaya XX sl.10, pp.202-205

cards.agreement: 1 book gives the yoga (PD); UK supports the 9th's weight. The defining sloka was seen only in the index this pass.

question_types: Why does money not stay with me?
Do I have a poverty yoga?
cards.rule: Caution flags, each with its cancellation: Kemadruma (no planet other than Sun in the 2nd or 12th from the Moon) - cancelled if any planet is in an angle from the Moon or Lagna or joins the Moon; the 2nd and 11th lords together in 6/8/12 with malefics in or aspecting 2 and 11; both lords combust or with malefics. These show pressure on money, not a verdict of poverty.
cards.agreement: 4 books carry the flags; BJ gives the cancellation explicitly. Books differ on Kemadruma cancellation details.
cards.convention: yes: Kemadruma cancellation list varies by text

question_types: Does my Hora chart support wealth?
cards.rule: The Hora (D2) is the division for wealth. Sun, Mars and Jupiter are at ease in the Sun's hora, Moon, Venus and Saturn in the Moon's hora, Mercury in either. Planets in their fitting hora add to wealth; the 2nd lord and Jupiter in a fitting hora are the key checks.

sources.location: Ch.I st.9 and notes, p.19; Ch.XXI st.4, pp.202-208

cards.agreement: 2 books give Hora a wealth role (BPHS directly, PD by weight); BJ uses it for strength. Modern D2 reading rules go beyond the texts.
cards.convention: yes: Parasari Sun/Moon hora vs cyclic hora

cards.rule: Indu Lagna (wealth point): add the kala numbers of the 9th lords from Lagna and from the Moon, count that many signs from the Moon. Benefics, exalted or vargottama planets in or aspecting Indu Lagna, and its lord strong, support asset growth.
cards.agreement: 1 book (UK), and its commentator says 'some astrologers'. Not found in the other four.
cards.convention: yes: kala numbers and inclusive counting

question_types: Will I be seen as wealthy?
Will my wealth be visible to others?
cards.rule: Strong planets in the Arudha Lagna (AL) and in the Dara pada (A7) make one wealthy and famous; A7 in the 6th, 8th or 12th from AL means thin means. Judge the Dhana pada (A2) and gains pada (A11) from the AL the same way (planets in the 2nd and 11th from AL are read as wealth in later practice).
cards.agreement: 2 books use arudhas; the AL/A7 wealth rule is BPHS only. '2nd/11th from AL' is later practice.
cards.convention: yes: arudha exception rule; which planets count as 'strong'

question_types: Which years are good for finances?
cards.rule: Use Ashtakavarga: the 2nd and 11th signs with high Sarvashtakavarga bindus (28 or more) and the 2nd/11th lords with 4 or more bindus in their own Bhinnashtakavarga signs show solid wealth support. Transits of Jupiter and Saturn through high-bindu signs from the Moon mark gain windows; low-bindu signs mark lean spells.

sources.location: Adhyaya XXIII sl.22, pp.265-266; XXIII sl.10-11 and XXIV sl.37-43 (index)

cards.agreement: 2 books agree on bindus modifying transit results. Thresholds (28 SAV, 4 BAV) are convention, not verse.
cards.convention: yes: bindu thresholds; reduced vs unreduced bindus for transit (UK says unreduced)

question_types: Will I have sudden gains or losses?
cards.rule: Patterns only, never advice: the 2nd lord in the 8th gives land and wealth through inheritance or bequest; the 8th lord in the 11th gives little wealth early and comfort later; a strong 8th lord's dasha clears debts; Rahu with Venus and a debilitated 2nd lord has shown trade prosperity in practice. Speculative gain is read from 5th-11th links and is to be stated as a tendency.
cards.agreement: 3 books agree that the 8th carries inheritance and sudden money; the Rahu-Venus-2nd-lord note is a commentator's observation, not a verse.

question_types: Will I own a house or land?
cards.rule: The 4th house links property to wealth. The 4th lord in its own or exaltation sign, or in the 4th, gives land, houses and vehicles; a 2nd-11th exchange where one lord also rules the 4th shows wealth from building and property. Purchases cluster in the dasha of the 4th lord or of planets in the 4th, and in Saturn's transit of the 3rd or 11th from the Moon.

sources.location: Ch.17 (4th House) v.3, pp.221-222; Ch.26 v.40, pp.293-295; Ch.15 example chart pp.203-205

cards.agreement: 3 books agree on the 4th as land and houses and on the 4th lord's dasha as the purchase time.
cards.convention: no (BPHS ch.17 v.10-14 vehicle-year rules are a separate, untested convention)

question_types: Is this period good for finances?
cards.rule: Money arrives in the dashas of the 2nd, 9th and 11th lords, of Jupiter and of the Lagna lord when those planets are strong by Shadbala (over 10 rupas very good, under 5 poor). A weak lord's dasha brings spending, debts and loss. Within a dasha, the lord's drekkana shows where the weight falls.

sources.location: Ch.47 v.5-6, Ch.48 v.1 (Santhanam pp.453, 465 per references.json)

cards.agreement: 3 books agree on dasha-lord strength deciding financial results; UK gives the rupa thresholds.
cards.convention: yes: Vimshottari start variant; Shadbala method approximations noted in strength.classical_shadbala notes

question_types: How strong is my money planet really?
cards.rule: Sharpen any wealth judgement with varga dignity: a 2nd lord or Jupiter that holds high dignity across many vargas (Vimshopaka score 15-20, or classical names like Gopuramsa/Paravatamsa) gives wealth, lands and houses; low scores (under 5) cannot deliver even when the rasi placement looks good.
cards.agreement: 2 books agree on varga-dignity counting; the point tables differ across texts (engine notes this).
cards.convention: yes: Vimshopaka weights and dignity-to-fraction mapping are convention_dependent (engine note)

cards.rule: Read learning from the 2nd (speech and vidya), 4th (schooling and formal learning) and 5th (intellect and memory), with the 9th for higher wisdom. Strong lords of 2, 4 and 5 in good houses, with benefics in or aspecting those houses, give sound and complete education; lords in 6/8/12 or afflicted show breaks and strain.
cards.agreement: 4 books name a learning house, but they do not name the same one: PD puts vidya in the 2nd, UK in the 4th and 5th, Saravali intelligence in the 5th, BPHS higher education with the 5th. Read all three (2, 4, 5).

question_types: Will I do well in exams?
cards.rule: Mercury is the planet of learning. Mercury in the Lagna, 4th or 5th, in its own or exaltation sign, and not badly combust, gives sharp intellect and learning in many subjects; in the 2nd it earns through talent and speech.

sources.location: Ch.4 (Mercury significations, per references.json); Ch.29 notes p.328

cards.agreement: 2 books agree (PD and Saravali); Saravali's Virgo note softens the combustion caution.

question_types: Will I go for higher studies?
Will I become a teacher or scholar?
cards.rule: Jupiter is the second planet of learning. Jupiter in the Lagna makes one learned; in the 5th intelligent; in the 9th a scholar or minister; Jupiter aspecting the Lagna or the 4th/5th lords supports higher studies. Jupiter in the 8th or 12th, or debilitated, weakens the support.
cards.agreement: 3 books agree on Jupiter's learning role.

question_types: Do I have a yoga for intelligence?
Will I be a writer or scholar?
cards.rule: Sun and Mercury together (Budhaditya) point to intellect and status; Sun, Moon and Mercury together to sharp intelligence and public service; Sun, Mercury and Jupiter together to scholarship, poetry and writing. Judge by the house and the dignity of Mercury.
cards.agreement: 1 book located (Saravali); BPHS carries Budhaditya per the rule set but it was not re-located.

question_types: Will I be learned and eloquent?
cards.rule: Saraswati yoga: Jupiter, Venus and Mercury each in an angle, trine or the 2nd house, with Jupiter in its own, exaltation or a friendly sign. It gives wide learning, eloquence, poetry and fame.

sources.location: Adhyaya VI sl.26-27 (index entry located, p.59 of index)

cards.agreement: 1 book located (PD); BPHS carries it per the rule set.

cards.rule: Benefics beside the Moon help the mind: Jupiter or Mercury in the 12th from the Moon (Anapha) gives knowledge of many sastras; Jupiter and Mercury on both sides of the Moon give learning and composition skill; benefics in the 6th-7th-8th from the Moon (Adhi yoga) give leadership. Kemadruma (no support) is a caution for focus, with its cancellations.

sources.location: Ch.13 sl.24 and Anapha results, pp.151-153

cards.agreement: 3 books agree on the lunar-support yogas; only Saravali ties them to learning explicitly.
cards.convention: yes: Adhi yoga count variants (UK: one to three benefics)

question_types: How deep will my learning go?
cards.rule: The Chaturvimsamsa (D24, Siddhamsa) is the division for learning. Read the D24 Lagna lord, Mercury's and Jupiter's dignity in D24, and planets in the D24 4th and 5th to judge depth and subject. Weigh it below the rasi chart.
cards.agreement: 1 book names D24 for learning (BPHS); PD only sets the weight. Specific D24 rules are modern.
cards.convention: yes: D24 counting (odd from Leo, even from Cancer is used); ayanamsa sensitivity at 1°15' boundaries

question_types: When will I finish my degree?
Which years are good for study?
When should I write the exam?
cards.rule: Study milestones fall in the dashas and antardashas of the 4th, 5th and 9th lords and of Mercury and Jupiter, when those planets are strong. A weak Mercury period dulls the intellect; a strong 5th lord period gives merit and a position of counsel; a strong 4th lord period gives higher status.
cards.agreement: 3 books agree on dasha-lord timing by house lordship and strength.

question_types: Is this a good year for my exam?
Will I clear the entrance test?
cards.rule: From the natal Moon, Jupiter in the 2nd, 5th, 9th or 11th and Mercury in the 4th, 6th, 10th or 11th support study and exam success; Jupiter in the 3rd, 4th, 8th or 10th and Saturn in the 4th or 5th strain concentration. Apply vedha and the Ashtakavarga bindus of the transited sign.
cards.agreement: 2 books (PD gives the houses, UK the Ashtakavarga modifier). The exam reading is a modern use of general gochara.

question_types: Why do my studies keep getting interrupted?
Will I lose interest in studies?
cards.rule: Caution flags, each softened by a benefic aspect or a strong Lagna lord: the 4th or 5th lord in 6/8/12 or combust; Saturn in the 4th or 5th; Ketu in the 2nd; Jupiter with Rahu or Ketu (Guru-Chandala); Mercury with Saturn. These show strain or a break, not denial of education.

sources.location: Adhyaya VIII sl.22 and sl.28, pp.92-97

cards.agreement: 2 books located; flags do not contradict each other.

cards.rule: Map the strongest of Mercury, Jupiter, Mars, Venus, Saturn, Sun and Moon (and the planets ruling or occupying the 4th, 5th and 10th, and the navamsa lord of the 10th lord) to fields: Mercury = maths, commerce, writing, computing; Jupiter = law, philosophy, finance, teaching; Mars = engineering, surgery, defence; Venus = arts, design, hospitality; Saturn = engineering, mining, labour sciences; Sun = administration, medicine; Moon = public service, psychology, nursing.
cards.agreement: 3 books give planet-to-field signatures, but the mapping to modern degrees is ours.

question_types: Will I clear a competitive exam?
Will I win against other candidates?
cards.rule: Competition is read from the 6th and 11th houses and from Mars and Saturn transits. A strong 6th lord's dasha overcomes rivals; Saturn transiting the 3rd, 6th or 11th from the Moon and Mars in the 3rd or 6th support contests; link these with EDU-08 and EDU-09 for the study side.

sources.location: Adhyaya XX sl.7, pp.202-205; Adhyaya XXVI sl.2, pp.286-288

cards.agreement: 1 book (PD). The use for competitive exams is modern.

question_types: which body part should I take care of
why does this body area trouble me
cards.rule: Signs map the body head (Aries) to feet (Pisces). The sign on the 6th, and the sign holding the 6th lord or malefics joined to it, names the body area to care for; also count the map from the lagna.
cards.agreement: 4 books on the map; BPHS alone ties it to the 6th lord

question_types: why do I have bone/skin/blood issues
cards.rule: Sun bones, Moon blood, Mars marrow, Mercury skin, Jupiter fat/brain, Venus reproductive fluid, Saturn nerves. An afflicted planet (debilitated, combust, in war, with Saturn/Rahu in 6/8/12) flags its tissue.
cards.agreement: 2 found, BPHS likely

cards.rule: Sun and Mars bilious (pitta); Moon windy-phlegmatic; Jupiter phlegmatic (kapha); Venus wind and phlegm; Saturn windy (vata); Mercury mixed. Lagna lord and strongest planet colour the constitution.

sources.location: ch.2 planet descriptions; ch.17 lagna results

question_types: why do I fall sick often
cards.rule: Disease tendency comes from planets in the 6th, planets in 8th and 12th, the 6th lord, and planets with the 6th lord. Speak only when two or more independent pointers agree.

question_types: what kind of health issue am I prone to
cards.rule: Planet in or ruling the 6th gives the flavour: Sun heat/eyes/heart; Moon fluids/sleep; Mars injury/blood/bile; Mercury skin/nerves; Jupiter digestion/fat/ears; Venus urinary/reproductive/anaemia; Saturn chronic/joints/wind. Never a diagnosis.
cards.agreement: PD full table; BPHS and BJ agree on Mars

question_types: why am I always slightly unwell
cards.rule: Lagna lord in 6th, or 6th lord in lagna, inclines to a sickly body; cancelled when that lord is exalted, own-sign or a natural benefic (then exercise-loving). 6th lord in 8th is the harder form.
Strong lagna lord in a kendra with benefic aspect, or strong Jupiter in the lagna, is the resilience baseline that softens other afflictions.

sources.location: Santhanam ch.17 v.9-12 Jupiter clause (references.json bphs17_9)

question_types: when should I be careful about health
why am I sick in this period
cards.rule: Extra-care periods: dasha/antar of the 6th lord, of weak planets in 6/8/12, of a badly placed lagna lord, of a weak 8th lord. A dignified dasha lord runs well even if it rules a dusthana.
cards.convention: yes: Tara start, ayanamsa near nakshatra boundary

question_types: is Sade Sati bad for my health
what does Ashtama Shani mean for me
cards.rule: Saturn over the Moon sign or 8th from it are periods to mind rest and chronic complaints; weight by Saturn's BAV, SAV, kakshya, Vedha and natal Saturn. Saturn 6th from the Moon is a good transit. Flag, not verdict.
cards.agreement: 1 classic plus South Indian tradition; the name Sade Sati not found in any OCR
cards.convention: yes: from natal Moon; Vedha school

question_types: how strong is this bad period
cards.rule: A planet transiting a sign where its BAV is 0-3 or SAV under 25 gives its hard side; PD says do shanti and discipline then. In dasha, a bhava suffers under lords placed in low-bindu houses.

sources.location: ch.23 sl.1; ch.26 sl.49; ch.15 sl.12 and ch.26 sl.41 (index)

cards.agreement: PD found; BPHS likely

cards.rule: Moon or lagna lord in a Jupiter/Venus/Mercury trimsamsa supports health; in Saturn's trimsamsa inclines to low energy; in Mars's to heat and injury.
cards.agreement: BJ effect; BPHS definition

cards.rule: Practice uses D6 lagna/6th to refine the disease picture; no classic in our corpus defines or uses D6.
cards.agreement: 0; not found in five books

cards.rule: Mars with or aspecting the 6th lord, Mars-Mercury link, or 8th lord in the lagna inclines to cuts, falls, accidents; care in Mars periods and Mars transits over lagna/6th.

sources.location: ch.19 notes; Santhanam ch.17 Mars clause and ch.24 v.85 (references.json)

cards.agreement: BPHS main; PD partial

question_types: which phase of life needs more care

cards.agreement: 2 books use the navamsa of the pada; the dharma/artha/kama/moksha gloss appears in none.

Modern authors (e.g. Harness, Sutton, Dennis) build 'Ardra = Rudra's storm = turbulence', 'Bharani = Yama = discipline and endings', 'Ashlesha = Nagas = clinging'. Treat these as story-telling: offer them as a reflection prompt, never as a classical claim.

question_types: is my star fixed, sharp, soft
cards.rule: Muhurta tradition sorts stars into Dhruva (fixed), Chara (movable), Kshipra (quick), Mridu (soft), Tikshna (sharp), Ugra (fierce), Mishra (mixed). This is for choosing times. Reading it as personality (Mridu = gentle person) is a modern extension; it is plausible and cheap to test.
cards.agreement: Tradition (Muhurta Chintamani, not in corpus); 0 of 5 use it for character.
cards.convention: Yes: Abhijit handling; class lists vary slightly.

question_types: which stars are good for me
cards.rule: Count from the birth star to any star, cycle of 9: 1 Janma, 2 Sampat, 3 Vipat, 4 Kshema, 5 Pratyak (Pratyari), 6 Sadhana (Sadhaka), 7 Naidhana (Vadha), 8 Mitra, 9 Parama Mitra (Ati-mitra). Sampat, Kshema, Sadhana, Mitra, Parama Mitra are favourable; Janma and Naidhana call for care; Vipat and Pratyak are mixed. Used with Chandrabala for the day's tone.
cards.agreement: 0 of 5 in OCR. The rule is from muhurta texts (Muhurta Chintamani, Kalaprakashika) and daily panchanga practice, i.e. long tradition but outside our corpus.
cards.convention: Yes: Janma/Vadha as 'care' vs all four odd taras as bad; some count 3 cycles with Janma tara of cycle 2/3 softer.

cards.rule: Modern practice: take the dasha (or antardasha) lord's natal nakshatra and count its tara from the birth star; Sampat/Kshema/Sadhana/Mitra lords run smoother, Vipat/Pratyak/Naidhana lords feel rough. Not in our classics, which judge dashas by the lord's dignity, house and avastha instead.
cards.agreement: 0 of 5 for tara-of-dasha-lord; 1 (BPHS) gives the classical alternative.
cards.convention: Yes: tara counting and which taras count as bad.

question_types: Can I trust what this planet promises?
cards.rule: Each planet needs a minimum Shadbala before you trust its promises: Sun 6.5, Moon 6, Mars 5, Mercury 7, Jupiter 6.5, Venus 5.5, Saturn 5 rupas. Below that, soften every claim about the houses it rules.

question_types: Is this a good dasha for me?
cards.rule: Read the dasha lord's strength before the house it rules. Exalted and strong lord gives a full period; a powerless lord an empty one; a lord in an enemy's navamsa a miserable one.
cards.agreement: 3 in OCR agree; BPHS by reference.

question_types: Is my planet steady across the chart?

cards.rule: Two planets (Mars to Saturn) within one degree are at war; the house whose lord loses gets weak results in that lord's dasha. Sun and Moon never fight.

question_types: What mood is this planet in?

question_types: My planet is vargottama, what does it mean?

question_types: My planet is debilitated, is it cancelled?
cards.rule: Five cancellations: debilitation-sign lord or planet exalted there in kendra from Lagna/Moon; debilitation and exaltation lords in mutual kendras; sign lord aspects the debilitated planet; exaltation-sign lord in kendra from Lagna/Moon; the debilitated planet itself in kendra from Lagna/Moon. A cancelled weakness, not a new strength.
cards.agreement: Phaladeepika full; BPHS mention; Saravali retrograde variant.
cards.convention: yes: aspect of sign lord; Moon as reference

question_types: My planet is retrograde, is it strong?
cards.rule: A retrograde planet has motion strength and gives much, even in a weak sign; but retrograde in exaltation gives little, by many authors.
